Let me look at the `mpz_init_set_str` loop more carefully. The issue might be with the `len` parameter. In vm.c:

```c
regs[a] = mrb_bint_new_str(mrb, s+2, (mrb_int)s[0], (mrb_int)s[1]);
```

Here `s[0]` is the length stored as a `char`. If the length is > 127, `s[0]` would be negative when cast to `mrb_int`. But `new_litbn` limits `plen` to 255, and `buf[0] = (char)plen`. So for `plen > 127`, `s[0]` would be negative.

Wait, but `new_litbn` checks `if (plen > 255) codegen_error(s, "integer too big")`. So `plen` can be up to 255. If `plen = 200`, then `buf[0] = (char)200 = -56` (as signed char). Then in vm.c, `(mrb_int)s[0] = -56`. So `len = -56` in `mpz_init_set_str`.

Then in the loop: `for (i = len-1;; i--)` with `len = -56`, so `i = -57`. Then `s[i]` reads `s[-57]` which is way before the string - that's an out-of-bounds read, potentially a heap-use-after-free!

But wait, `new_litbn` checks `plen > 255`, so `plen` can be up to 255. But `buf[0] = (char)plen` - for `plen > 127`, this becomes negative. So a bigint literal with more than 127 digits would trigger this.

Actually wait, let me re-check. `buf[0] = (char)plen` where `plen` is `size_t`. If `plen = 200`, then `(char)200` in C is implementation-defined but typically wraps to `200 - 256 = -56`. So `s[0] = -56` as a signed char.

Then in vm.c: `(mrb_int)s[0] = -56`. So `len = -56` in `mpz_init_set_str`.

In the loop: `for (i = len-1;; i--)` → `i = -57`. Then `s[i]` = `s[-57]` reads 57 bytes before the string start. That's an out-of-bounds read.

But wait, `mrb_assert(2 <= iabs(base) && iabs(base) <= 36)` in `mrb_bint_new_str`. For a negative bigint, `s[1] = 0x80 = -128`, so `iabs(-128) = 128` which is > 36. That would fail the assert!

Hmm, but asserts might be disabled in release builds. Let me check if `mrb_assert` is a no-op in release mode.

Actually, let me reconsider. The `base` in `mpz_init_set_str` is `s[1]`. For a negative bigint, `s[1] = 0x80 = -128`. Then in `mpz_init_set_str`:

```c
if (*s == '-') {
    sn = -1; s++;
}
else if (base < 0) {          /* trick: negative if base < 0 */
    sn = -1; base = -base;
}
```

So `base = -(-128) = 128`. Then `mpz_init_set_int(mrb,&bb, base)` with `base = 128`. Then in the loop, `if (k >= base)` - digits are 0-9, so `k < 10 < 128`, fine.

But `mrb_assert(2 <= iabs(base) && iabs(base) <= 36)` in `mrb_bint_new_str` would fail since `iabs(-128) = 128 > 36`. Unless asserts are disabled.

Let me check how `mrb_assert` is defined:

<｜｜DSML｜｜=execute_bash>
<｜｜DSML｜｜=command>grep -rn "define mrb_assert" /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/include/ | head -5</｜｜DSML｜｜>
</｜｜DSML｜｜>
